title: Why won't subtitles open my file?
fullTitle: FFmpeg subtitles Filter Path Escaping: 3 of 12 Open the Wrong File

scenes.narration: You write subtitles equals and a file name, and the filter cannot open it, or opens another file and says nothing. Which characters in a path break it? Twelve paths, six ways to write each, every frame read twice, on f f m peg six point one point one.
captions: subtitles=NAME: cannot open it, or opens another.

scenes.narration: A gray frame and twelve subtitle files, each with its own text, so the pixels name the file that was opened. Reader one: the decoded frame in Node. Reader two: the frame md five from f f m peg. Controls: no subtitles, and a safe name. No shell.
captions: 12 files, one text each, so pixels name the file.

scenes.narration: Written as is, three paths work: a plain name, a space, a space in a folder. Six stop with an error: colon, brackets, comma, semicolon, equals sign, and a folder named C colon. Three open the wrong file with no error: an apostrophe, a backslash, an apostrophe in a folder.
captions: As is: 3 work, 6 error, 3 open the wrong file.

scenes.narration: Why: the string is read twice. First as a filter graph, where a comma, semicolon or bracket ends the arguments. Then as options, where a colon starts the next option and an apostrophe is a quote. The error names the leftover. The apostrophe is simply eaten, so another file opens.
captions: Read twice: filter graph, then options.
The error names the leftover piece.

scenes.narration: One level of backslashes fixes nothing: thirty six rows, same as raw. Quotes fix brackets, comma and semicolon only. Two levels, backslash backslash before a colon, fix all but the equals sign, which needs its own. A relative name with a colon also needs dot slash: the text before the colon reads as a protocol.
captions: One level: same as raw in 36 of 36 rows.
Two levels, = escaped, ./ in front: 12 of 12.

scenes.narration: The shell is a third layer. Bare or in double quotes, backslash backslash colon loses a level and fails; in single quotes it works. So: two levels, dot slash, single quotes, or a safe name. Not tested: Windows paths, other builds, other libass versions, non ASCII names.
captions: Single quotes. Two levels. ./ for a colon.
